To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-12 and/or IL-18, in the presence of tissue injury, induce IFN-gamma, resulting in the expression of MHC class molecules.

tissue injury as a consequence from ischemia followed by subsequent reperfusion induces IL-12 and subsequently IL-18, which in turn induce IFN-gamma, which up-regulates MHC class I expression in the injured tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the cytokine network during ischemia/reper fusion-induced inflammation.
the induction of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-18 and IL-12 in the kidney following ischemia/reper fusion.
the role of IL-12/IL-18/IFN-gamma axis in ischemia/reper fusion-induced up-regulation of the MHC class I/II Ags, which are involved in the initiation and maintenance of the adaptive immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-12 and/or IL-18, in addition to their known role in the immune response to microbial infections, also play a role in the inflammatory response to tissue damage.

the ischemia-induced up-regulation of IL-12, and to a lesser extent of IL-18, leads to the production of endogenous IFN-gamma, which in turn is responsible for the induction of MHC Ag up-regulation in the injured kidney.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ischemia/reper fusion injury of the kidney induces IL-12, which in turn up-regulates IL-18.
the induction of IL18 and IL-12 after tissue damage is a novel aspect of the immune response to nonmicrobial injury.
ischemia induces IL-18 and IL-12, which in turn induce IFN-gamma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-12 and especially IL-18 are involved in the IFN-gama response to ischemia/reperfusions.
tissue injury can be a source of endogenous IL-18 and IL-12, and these cytokines are capable of inducing IFN-gamma in a synergistic fashion.
tissue injury, as a result of ischemia, can induce IL-12 as a consequence of IL-18 and IL-18 as a consequence of caspase- 1 activation.
